indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm/decide whether argparse refusing a flag-looking following token for --reason/--class/--caused-by/--ref/--assignee is an acceptable behavior change vs the old unconditional next-token capture.
evidence: Original loop: `elif a == "--reason": ... assignee = args[i + 1]` consumed the next token unconditionally regardless of whether it began with '--'

New: `parser.add_argument("--reason", default="")` + `parser.parse_known_args(rest)` — argparse will not treat a recognized option token as `--reason`'s value and instead triggers error() -> CommandError
Commit message: 'WITHOUT changing observable behavior' and 'exact-token comparison'
indeterminate.finding: argparse refuses a following token that is itself a registered option as a flag value, whereas the retired loop consumed the next token unconditionally. E.g. `--reason --class=x` previously set reason='--class=x' (and skipped nothing else); now it raises 'Error: --reason requires a value'. This is an observable behavior change contrary to the commit's stated no-behavior-change goal.
scenarios: Operator runs `rebar transition <id> open closed --reason --force=...` or `--reason --class=regression` (space-separated --reason with a following flag)

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the pre-extraction of --force does not change force-gate semantics for argv where a space-separated --reason precedes --force.
evidence: `_extract_force` loops the whole args list and pulls out every `--force`/`--force=` regardless of what precedes it
Original loop was a single ordered pass where `--reason` (bare) took `args[i+1]` before `--force` could be matched
force_reason None-vs-"" 'drives the close-gate bypass' per the docstring at transition.py:190
indeterminate.finding: `_extract_force` strips `--force`/`--force=<r>` from argv positionally-independently BEFORE argparse runs, but the original single left-to-right loop could have a space-separated `--reason` immediately preceding `--force` swallow `--force` as its reason value (force NOT triggered). Now `--reason --force` yields force_reason='' (bypass ON) and rest=['--reason'] -> 'requires a value' error. The force/close-gate bypass semantics differ for this argv.
scenarios: `rebar transition <id> ... --reason --force` — an ambiguous but previously-parseable argv now flips force on and errors differently

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the argparse switch does not silently reject previously-valid space-form values that begin with `--` (e.g. `--assignee --temp`), and add a test pinning whichever behavior is intended.
evidence: Old loop (diff, claim._parse_assignee): `elif a == "--assignee": ... assignee = args[i + 1]` took the next token unconditionally

New: `parser.add_argument("--assignee", default=None); ns, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args(args)` (claim.py:63-65) — argparse will not bind a following `--`-prefixed token as the value and instead calls error() -> CommandError exit 1
transition._parse_flags builds `--reason`/`--class`/`--caused-by`/`--ref` the same way (transition.py:154-158), so their space-form values that begin with `--` are likewise now rejected
Space form is a documented, supported convention: tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli_space_form_options.py:6 names `claim --assignee <you>`
ABSENCE: no test in tests/ pins the old dash-prefixed space-form value behavior (search of `--assignee`/`--reason` callsites shows only non-dash values), so the divergence is uncaught
indeterminate.finding: For the space-separated form, argparse-backed parsers narrow accepted input versus the retired loops: the old loops consumed the following token unconditionally as the value (so `--assignee --force` yielded assignee="--force", and `--reason --anything` yielded reason="--anything"), whereas the new `parse_known_args` refuses to consume a following token that looks like an option and instead triggers the `error()` override -> `CommandError` exit 1 ("requires a value"). A previously-accepted value that begins with `--` is now rejected.
scenarios: An operator (or wrapper) passes an assignee/reason/ref value that begins with `--` via the space form, e.g. `claim <id> --assignee --temp`; previously bound the literal value, now exits 1 with 'requires a value'
